newsitem.title: USA: Entergy sees 5 pct or better profit growth.
newsitem.headline: Entergy sees 5 pct or better profit growth.

text.p: Entergy Corp Chief Executive Ed Lupberger said on Thursday that over the near term he expects at least five percent annual growth in earnings before charges.
He also told a meeting with security analysts that he expects Entergy to be ready for retail competition when it comes.

"We have analyzed the steps we must take to prosper in a competitive market and have put a plan in place to get us there," he said, according to a company statement. Reporters were not allowed to attend the meeting.
"Successful execution of this plan will put us in a solid competitive position," he said.
The company has begun "regulatory initiatives designed to assure that our nuclear generation costs are fully competitive at the end of a seven-year transition period," Lupberger said.

"I expect annual growth in ongoing earnings of five percent or better over the next three years. Growth in our diversified businesses is expected to enable us to maintain superior total returns and offset any downside from transition issues in the longer term."
Lupberger said Entergy remains committed to delivering a total return to shareholders in the top quartile of U.S. electric companies.

Chief Financial Officer Gerald McInvale said Entergy's sales of electricity have been strong. "Megawatt-hour sales have grown about three percent on average over the past five years and we expect them to continue in that general range," he said.
Commenting on productivity improvements, he said the trend toward lower operation and maintenance expenses will continue.
"Since 1993 we have cut O&M expenses by about $80 million and expect a further reduction in the two percent range this year," he said.

McInvale said Entergy expects its strong cash flow to continue over the next three years. Noting operating cash flow was nearly $1.4 billion in 1995, he said that "we will manage that to improve our balance sheets and provide funds for sustained investment in growth opportunities."
"We expect to have approximately $2.5 billion available for dividends and growth investments in the 1996-98 timeframe," he said.
McInvale said Entergy's diversified growth businesses are on the way to becoming positive contributors.
"In 1996, although Entergy Power Group is expected to be profitable, we expect the total diversified group to lose in the $15 million range. This compares to a loss of $44 million in 1995," he said..
"In 1997 we expect this group to contribute profits in the $20 to $30 million range and in 1998 more than $100 million.
"We expect the diversified businesses to continue growing as we make further investments and realize our target investment returns in the 15 percent range."
